A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mean-estimation work. Their complete text, algorithms, equations, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports algorithms, mathematical guarantees, and proofs, but no original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical. Its added generalization and empirical-mean results are mathematical statements and proofs, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 replaces an independent empirical-mean initialization with the coordinate-wise median of the existing sample means. Its prescribed iteration count decreases from order log(1/δ) to order log log(1/δ). Algorithm 3 also adds a singleton stopping condition.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios for experimental evaluation. The bounded-distribution setting introduced in v3 is an analytical extension.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Comparisons with the empirical mean and earlier algorithms concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental protocols, evaluation metrics, or training settings. Changes to algorithmic constants and iteration bounds are theoretical specifications.

E4.justification: Neither version contains experimental ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or case studies. The illustrations and constructed instances support mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, or significance tests. Revised failure-probability calculations belong to the theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: No measured numerical or qualitative outcomes appear in either PDF. The changed running-time and sample-complexity guarantees are theoretical results.

T1.justification: v3 adds initialization Lemma 3.5, generalization Corollary 3.8, and empirical-mean lower-bound Theorem 5.2. It substantially revises the gradient analysis, changing the contraction factor from 0.99 to 0.7 and the convergence/stability radii from 14r/16r to 10r/11r. MinSumSelect's recurrence is also corrected. However, the new initialization proof contains a displayed inequality that is invalid as written.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions strengthen the gradient algorithm's running-time claim from O((ε^-1 + log(1/δ)) log(1/δ) d) to O((ε^-1 + log log(1/δ)) log(1/δ) d). Both algorithms are now described as nearly optimal in time. Section 1.1 also adds an optimal Θ(log(1/δ)/|S|) generalization-rate claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds a statistical interpretation through excess risk for distributions supported on the unit ball, contrasting its rate with geometric-median and k-means learning rates. Remark 3.7 strengthens the earlier pessimistic-outlier discussion by asserting that worst-case instances justify it. Remark 4.6 newly states that exponential dependence on recursion depth is unavoidable.

D1.justification: For gradient descent, v2 specifies groups of 4a/ε with sufficient constants a≥256 and b≥1086; v3 specifies a/ε with a=1440 and b=50. v3 also documents linear-time rank selection for the coordinate-wise initialization and projected medians. These are algorithm specifications, not experimental settings.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around statistical mean estimation and clustering generalization, adding works including Bartlett et al., Bucarelli et al., Klochkov et al., and Lugosi–Mendelson (2024). It also adds discussion of Musco et al.'s dimension-dependent mean-estimation bound and revises the account of prior power-mean bounds.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related work, and much of the existing algorithm exposition are rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around convergence, stability, and initialization, while Section 5 becomes two lower-bound subsections. Algorithm names, section titles, and the author list also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting, extensively reflowing equations and algorithm blocks. Figure 1 changes from two side-by-side cases on v2 page 6 to one redrawn diagram on v3 page 5, with additional projection labels and an emphasized bounded projection segment.

improvement.justification: v3's new initialization, generalization discussion, and empirical-mean lower bound substantially extend v2's treatment. However, new Lemma 3.5 bounds error from the true mean by distances to two bounding good means, an inequality that can fail even in one dimension. This lemma supports the faster-runtime claim. The substantive additions therefore coexist with a gap in their written justification, making the net quality direction uncertain.
